subject: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines

Team —

Quick summary and ask: LumenHealth (pilot + multi-year expansion) wants a 30% first-year committed discount and three contract redlines that our standard playbook flags as high-risk: (1) an MFN clause covering all SaaS + model pricing for 24 months, (2) a benchmark clause tying our unit price to a named competitor index, and (3) a provision that would restrict Redwood from offering prioritized feature access to certain public cloud partners in North America for the 12-month pilot (a de-facto regional exclusivity).

Commercials: ARR (run-rate if converted): $1.2M. Committed spend year one: $420k (after requested discount). Term: 36 months with annual true-ups. They want signature by 6/15 to align with their board cycle.

Requesting: Exec guidance/approval on a one-time exception envelope. Proposed counter (my recommendation):
- Discount: Approve up to 25% year-1, tapering to standard list by year 3; provide an additional usage-based rebate for volume above 10M tokens/month.
- MFN: Limit scope to the specific product SKU (hosted inference API) and exclude marketplace/partner resell channels; reduce duration to 12 months.
- Benchmark: Convert to a non-binding benchmarking reference with a floor (no downward price adjustment) and an annual reconciliation window instead of automatic repricing.
- Exclusivity-like language: Reject any geographic or partner exclusivity; allow a limited pilot commitment for feature prioritization (30 days notice to opt out).

Attachments: redlines (pdf) and commercial summary (xlsx). Legal flagged the MFN and benchmark as high risk for revenue leakage and for setting a price reference that’s hard to unwind.

Timeline: We need a decision by EOD 5/22 so I can get revised terms back to LumenHealth before their executive procurement call Tuesday.

Appreciate a quick read — I can jump on a 20-min sync at 10:30 if helpful.

Thanks,
Grace
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines

Grace — thanks for the summary and the attachments. Read Legal's comments and ran the numbers with Finance. A few clarifying points before I escalate to execs:

1) Is the requested 30% net of existing promotional credits? The commercial sheet indicates a $50k one-time onboarding credit — confirm whether that is additional.
2) Can Lumen agree to a 12-month MFN instead of 24, and to limit the MFN to list price comparisons (i.e., not to include partner discounts or transitory pilot promos)?
3) For the benchmark clause: which competitor(s) did they name in the redline? If it's a named sole competitor we should push to an index or remove naming.

From a deal-desk POV: Approving a 25% cap + MFN carveouts seems acceptable if we get an exec signoff committing the legal guardrails you outlined. If you're comfortable, I'll draft the escalation note to the revenue execs and include a recommended conditional approval (25% + MFN limited to product SKU + 12 months + benchmark non-binding).

If you can confirm answers to (1)-(3) I will prepare the note and loop in VP Revenue and CFO for sign-off.

Karthik
Sr. Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines

Karthik — answers inline:
1) The 30% was net of the $50k onboarding credit (so total customer economic is effectively 32% in year 1 if we include the credit). We should treat the credit as one-time and exclude from MFN scope.
2) They verbally signaled openness to 12 months but put 24 in the redline. We can likely land 12 months with the right framing.
3) Benchmark: they named two competitors by name (BorealisAI and Nimbus Labs) and requested automatic parity adjustments if their published list rates change.

Confirmed: I agree to escalate with your recommended conditional approval. Please prepare the escalation to the execs (Ben and VP Revenue + CFO). I'd like the note to emphasize the commercial value (strategic pilot in an id-med cluster, references, and expansion motion) and propose the precise legal language Karthik suggested (MFN scoped to SKU and list price only; benchmark as non-binding reference with floor).

I'll copy the external procurement lead once we have a conditional term sheet.

Grace
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, VP Revenue <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 13:32:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines

Ben (and Revenue leadership) — escalating for quick exec decision. TL;DR: LumenHealth asks for a 30% year-1 discount + MFN (24 months) + named-competitor benchmark + implied pilot exclusivity. Risk: revenue leakage and precedent-setting for MFN/benchmark clauses; operational risk if benchmark triggers automatic repricing.

Recommended conditional approval (what Deal Desk proposes):
- Approve up to 25% discount year-1 (net of the $50k onboarding credit). Discount to ratchet to list by year 3.
- MFN: limit to the specific product SKU (hosted inference API), apply only to direct list price comparisons (exclude partner/reseller/marketplace offers), duration 12 months.
- Benchmark: change to a non-binding benchmarking reference; include a floor equal to 85% of current list and require annual reconciliation (no automatic mechanical repricing).
- Exclusivity: reject any broad exclusivity; allow a 90-day prioritized pilot support window capped at specific feature requests; must be mutually agreed and revocable.

If approved, Legal will issue precise redline language and I will send the conditional term sheet back to the customer. Financial impact (NPV) is estimated but acceptable given reference value and expansion runway.

Ask: Ben (and CFO if present), can you confirm by EOD 5/22? If yes, please reply-all with your conditional sign-off so I can finalize with Legal and get a countersigned term sheet out.

Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Exec approval for LumenHealth pricing exception & MFN/benchmark redlines

Thanks for the tight summary. I approve the deal-desk recommended envelope CONDITIONALLY on these T&Cs being reflected in the term sheet and Legal sign-off:
- 25% max year-1 discount (net of onboarding credit) with a structured ramp back to list by year 3.
- MFN restricted to product SKU, list-price-only comparisons, and 12-month duration. MFN must explicitly exclude transient promotional offers and any partner/resale channels.
- Benchmark clause converted to a non-binding reference with an explicit floor (85% of current list) and an annual reconciliation window; no automatic downward repricing.
- No enforceable geographic or partner exclusivity; limit prioritized pilot support to a 90-day mutually agreed scope.

Once Legal returns clean redlines to those terms, give them the conditional term sheet and loop procurement. Grace — please send the revised term sheet to Emma and procurement and copy Legal. Karthik — I'll follow up with finance to update forecast assumptions.

Ben Carter
VP, Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
